hints.title: Bidirectional Friendship Union
hints.text: Friendship is symmetric. Each accepted request contributes one friend to both the requester and the accepter.

hints.title: Union All Participant Stacking
hints.text: Combine requester_id and accepter_id into a single unified column of participant IDs by vertically stacking accepted records. Then group by participant and count occurrences.

hints.title: Most Friends Blueprint
hints.text: With Friends as (select requester_id as id from RequestAccepted union all select accepter_id as id from RequestAccepted) select id, count(*) as num from Friends group by id order by num desc limit 1.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
WITH AllFriends AS (
    SELECT requester_id AS id FROM RequestAccepted
    UNION ALL
    SELECT accepter_id AS id FROM RequestAccepted
)
SELECT id, COUNT(*) AS num
FROM AllFriends
GROUP BY id
ORDER BY num DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

complexity.notes: Union all and grouping by participant executes in linear-logarithmic sorting time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Counting only requester or accepter separately misses reciprocal friendships.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: UNION ALL preserves duplicates without dedup overhead before grouping.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use of UNION ALL rather than UNION to properly tally both endpoints of a friendship.
